blocks.text: After the Mauryas, the north-west saw a succession of foreign powers — **Indo-Greeks, Shakas, Parthians and Kushans**. The **Kushans**, peaking under **Kanishka**, built a **Central-Asia-to-Ganga empire**, championed **Mahayana Buddhism and Gandhara-Mathura art**, and controlled the **Silk Route**.

rows: First to issue **gold coins** & **coins with king's portraits**; **Menander (Milinda)** — Buddhist (Milindapanho with Nagasena); introduced **Hellenistic (Gandhara) art**.
**Rudradaman I** — Junagadh inscription (first long Sanskrit inscription); repaired Sudarshana lake; Saka era.
**Kanishka (c. 78 CE)** — greatest; started the **Saka Era (78 CE)**; capital **Purushapura (Peshawar)** & Mathura.
**4th Buddhist Council (Kashmir)** → Mahayana; patronised **Ashvaghosha, Nagarjuna, Charaka, Vasumitra**.

items: Kanishka = Saka Era (78 CE) + 4th Council + Mahayana + Gandhara art — the essential cluster.
Indo-Greeks = first gold coins & portrait coins; Menander converted by Nagasena.

prelimsPointers: **Indo-Greeks** — first to issue **gold coins** and **portrait coins** in India.
**Menander (Milinda)** — Indo-Greek king; his dialogue with **Nagasena** = **Milindapanho**.
**Rudradaman I (Shaka)** — **Junagadh rock inscription** (first major **Sanskrit** inscription); repaired **Sudarshana lake**.
**Kanishka** — greatest Kushan; started the **Saka Era (78 CE)**; capital **Purushapura (Peshawar)**.
**4th Buddhist Council** held in **Kashmir** under Kanishka → rise of **Mahayana**.
Kanishka's court — **Ashvaghosha (Buddhacharita), Nagarjuna, Charaka (medicine), Vasumitra**.
**Gandhara art** = Greco-Roman + Buddhist; **Mathura art** = indigenous red sandstone.
mainsAngles: Assess the cultural contributions of the Kushans under Kanishka.

glossary.definition: The calendar era beginning 78 CE, associated with Kanishka and now India's national calendar.
A Greco-Roman-influenced Buddhist sculptural school of the north-west under the Kushans.
'The Questions of Milinda' — a dialogue between the Indo-Greek king Menander and the monk Nagasena.

blocks.text: The **Satavahanas (c. 1st BCE–3rd CE)** were the **first major Deccan power** after the Mauryas, ruling from **Pratishthana (Paithan)**. They revived **Brahmanism, patronised Buddhism (Amaravati), promoted maritime (Roman) trade**, and issued **lead & potin coins** — bridging north and south India.

rows: Founder **Simuka**; greatest **Gautamiputra Satakarni** (defeated the Shakas — Nasik prashasti of **Gautami Balasri**).
**Matronymic** names (Gautamiputra, Vasishthiputra); feudal 'ratika/maharathi' chiefs; **land grants to Brahmins/monks (first)**.
Flourishing **Roman trade** (ports, coins); guilds (shreni); **lead, potin, copper coins**.
**Prakrit** official language; **Hala's Gathasaptashati**; **Amaravati stupa** art; caves at Nasik, Karle.

items: First Deccan empire; Gautamiputra Satakarni + Nasik prashasti (Gautami Balasri); Amaravati + Roman trade.
First rulers to make land grants (tax-free) to Brahmins/monks — an important MCQ.

prelimsPointers: Satavahana founder **Simuka**; capital **Pratishthana (Paithan)**.
**Gautamiputra Satakarni** — greatest; destroyer of Shakas; praised in **Gautami Balasri's Nasik prashasti**.
**Matronymic** naming (named after mother) reflects women's status.
First dynasty to grant **tax-free land (agrahara)** to Brahmins & Buddhist monks.
**Prakrit** was the official language; **Hala** wrote **Gathasaptashati**.
Coins — mainly **lead & potin**; brisk **Indo-Roman trade** (Periplus of the Erythraean Sea).
Art — **Amaravati stupa**; rock-cut caves at **Nasik, Karle, Kanheri**.
mainsAngles: Discuss the Satavahanas as a bridge between north and south Indian culture.

glossary.definition: Naming a person after the mother (e.g. Gautamiputra), a distinctive Satavahana practice.
A tax-free land grant to Brahmins, first regularly made by the Satavahanas.
A Prakrit lyric anthology attributed to the Satavahana king Hala.

sections.heading: The Sangam Age — society, literature & economy

blocks.text: The **Sangam Age (c. 300 BCE–300 CE)** was the classical era of the **Tamil south**, ruled by the **three crowned kings — Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas**. Its **Sangam literature** (Tamil academies at Madurai) is the primary source, revealing a **prosperous trade economy and a distinctive Tamil society**.

rows: **Chera (bow emblem, Vanji), Chola (tiger, Uraiyur/Kaveripattinam), Pandya (fish, Madurai)**.
Three Sangams (academies) at **Madurai** under Pandya patronage; most works from the **third Sangam**.
Rich **Roman trade** (Muziris port; Roman gold coins); pearls, spices, muslin; guilds.

items: Cheras-Cholas-Pandyas with emblems & capitals; Tolkappiyam + twin epics + Tirukkural.
Roman trade via Muziris (Roman gold coins) is a favourite economy fact.

prelimsPointers: Three Sangam kingdoms — **Chera (bow, Vanji), Chola (tiger, Uraiyur), Pandya (fish, Madurai)**.
Sangams (Tamil academies) held at **Madurai** under **Pandya** patronage.
**Tolkappiyam** — oldest Tamil grammar; **Ettuthogai** (8 anthologies) & **Pattuppattu** (10 idylls).
Twin epics — **Silappadikaram (Ilango Adigal)** & **Manimekalai (Sattanar)**.
**Tirukkural** (Thiruvalluvar) — Tamil ethical classic ('Tamil Veda').
**Roman trade** via **Muziris** port; hoards of **Roman gold coins**; exports pearls, spices, muslin.
Land divided into five **tinais** (ecological-poetic zones).
mainsAngles: Describe Sangam literature as a source for early Tamil history and society.

glossary.definition: A literary academy of Tamil poets held at Madurai; the age and its literature take their name from it.
The earliest extant Tamil grammar, a key Sangam-age text.
One of five ecological-cum-poetic landscapes in Sangam Tamil literary convention.

blocks.text: The **Sunga dynasty (185–73 BCE)**, founded by **Pushyamitra Sunga** after assassinating the last Maurya, marked a **Brahmanical revival** and is famed for the **Bharhut and Sanchi stupa art** and the patronage of Sanskrit (Patanjali).

rows: **Pushyamitra Sunga** — a Maurya general who killed **Brihadratha (185 BCE)**; capital Pataliputra/Vidisha.
**Brahmanical revival**; performed **Ashvamedha** sacrifices; yet Buddhist art flourished.
**Bharhut & Sanchi stupa** railings/gateways (torana) enlarged; Heliodorus pillar (Besnagar).
Erected by a **Greek envoy (Heliodorus)** dedicated to **Vasudeva (Vishnu)** — early Bhagavatism.

items: Pushyamitra Sunga killed Brihadratha; Ashvamedha revival; Bharhut/Sanchi art; Patanjali's Mahabhashya.
Heliodorus pillar = early evidence of Vaishnava (Bhagavata) worship.

prelimsPointers: **Pushyamitra Sunga** founded the dynasty by killing the last Maurya **Brihadratha (185 BCE)**.
Sungas performed **Ashvamedha**; represent a **Brahmanical/Sanskrit revival**.
**Bharhut & Sanchi** stupa gateways (toranas) & railings developed in this period.
**Patanjali** wrote the **Mahabhashya** (commentary on Panini) at Pushyamitra's court.
**Heliodorus pillar (Besnagar/Vidisha)** — by a Greek envoy, dedicated to **Vasudeva**, evidences early **Bhagavatism**.
The Sungas were succeeded by the **Kanvas**.
mainsAngles: Evaluate the Sunga period as an age of Brahmanical revival and artistic growth.

glossary.definition: The Vedic horse sacrifice revived by the Sungas to assert Brahmanical kingship.
A pillar at Besnagar erected by a Greek envoy dedicated to Vasudeva, evidencing early Vaishnavism.
Patanjali's great commentary on Panini's Sanskrit grammar, composed in the Sunga age.

blocks.text: The **Gupta Empire (c. 319–550 CE)** ushered in a **'Classical/Golden Age'**. Founded by **Chandragupta I** and expanded by **Samudragupta and Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya)**, it featured a **decentralised administration, land-grant economy, revived Hinduism, and unmatched cultural achievement**.

rows: **Chandragupta I** (Gupta era 319-20 CE, Lichchhavi marriage), **Samudragupta** ('Napoleon of India' — Allahabad/Prayag Prashasti by **Harishena**), **Chandragupta II 'Vikramaditya'** (defeated Shakas; Fa-Hien visited; Navaratnas).
More **decentralised/feudal** than Mauryan; provinces (bhukti) → district (vishaya) → village; **land grants (agrahara)** rise.
Peak of **gold coins ('dinara')**; land revenue ~1/6; guilds; decline of long-distance trade later.
Rigid caste; **rise of untouchability & decline in women's status (early marriage, sati at Eran-510 CE)**.

items: Samudragupta = Prayag Prashasti (Harishena); Chandragupta II = Vikramaditya, Fa-Hien, Navaratnas.
Gold coins peak, feudal land-grants, first sati inscription (Eran 510) — society/economy markers.

prelimsPointers: **Gupta Era started 319-320 CE** (Chandragupta I); he married Lichchhavi princess **Kumaradevi**.
**Samudragupta** — 'Napoleon of India' (V.A. Smith); **Allahabad/Prayag Prashasti** composed by **Harishena** (Sanskrit).
**Chandragupta II 'Vikramaditya'** — defeated Shakas; **Fa-Hien (Faxian)** visited; court of **Navaratnas** (Kalidasa etc.).
Gupta **gold coins = 'dinara'**; the finest gold coinage in ancient India.
First epigraphic evidence of **sati** — **Eran inscription (510 CE)**.
Administration was more **feudal/decentralised**; increasing **land grants**.
**Mehrauli Iron Pillar** (Delhi) — rust-resistant, Gupta metallurgy (Chandra).
mainsAngles: Why is the Gupta age called the 'Golden Age' of ancient India? Critically examine.

glossary.definition: The Allahabad pillar inscription by Harishena eulogising Samudragupta's conquests.
The gold coin of the Gupta empire, marking the peak of ancient Indian gold coinage.
The 'nine gems' — scholars traditionally said to adorn Chandragupta II's court, including Kalidasa.

sections.heading: Gupta art, architecture, literature, science & technology

blocks.text: The Gupta age was the **classical peak of Indian culture** — the **first structural Hindu temples (Nagara), the Ajanta murals, Sanskrit literature (Kalidasa), and pioneering science (Aryabhata) and metallurgy (the rustless Iron Pillar)**.

rows: **First structural temples** — **Dashavatara temple (Deogarh), Bhitargaon (brick)**; **Nagara** style begins; **Nalanda University** (Kumaragupta).
**Aryabhata** (Aryabhatiya — zero-place value, earth's rotation, π); **Varahamihira (Brihatsamhita)**; **Brahmagupta**; **Sushruta/Charaka** medicine.
**Mehrauli Iron Pillar** — rust-free; advanced iron technology.

items: First structural temples (Deogarh) + Nagara style + Nalanda; Kalidasa in literature; Aryabhata & Varahamihira in science.

prelimsPointers: **Dashavatara temple, Deogarh** & brick **Bhitargaon** — earliest structural Hindu temples (**Nagara** style).
**Nalanda University** founded by **Kumaragupta I**.
**Kalidasa** — Abhijnanashakuntalam, Meghaduta, Raghuvamsha, Kumarasambhava.
**Aryabhata** — Aryabhatiya; concept of **zero/place-value, earth's rotation, value of π**; **Varahamihira** — Brihatsamhita.
**Ajanta paintings** (fresco/tempera) largely of the Gupta-Vakataka period.
**Mehrauli Iron Pillar** — rust-resistant, testament to Gupta **metallurgy**.
**Puranas, Dharmashastras (Smritis)** and the two epics reached final form in this era.
mainsAngles: Assess the achievements of the Gupta age in science, literature and art.

glossary.definition: The north-Indian temple architectural style whose earliest structural examples are Gupta.
Aryabhata's mathematical-astronomical treatise introducing place-value and the earth's rotation.
A Gupta-era rust-resistant iron pillar in Delhi, evidence of advanced metallurgy.
